2_Introduction: The PSC device gives the highest PCE of 16.0482%, with VOC of 1.0353 V, JSC of 23.717 mA/cm², and FF of 65.3602%. A 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 precursor solution was similarly prepared using a mixture of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. To promote better film morphology, 160 µL of antisolvent was added at last 6 s in the latter spin-coating step. The films were dried inside an N2 environment on a hot plate at a temperature of 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression enabled by the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ stoichiometry—where the mixed A-site cation ensemble optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppresses phase segregation under thermal stress, and mitigates halide vacancy formation while narrowing the bandgap to ~1.58 eV for enhanced visible absorption; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) in DMF:DMSO solvent ensures sufficient solute availability without premature nucleation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed deposition (1000 rpm, 10 s) enabling uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed crystallization (5000 rpm, 30 s) with antisolvent quenching at the critical 6-s mark—imposes a sharp supersaturation gradient that kinetically favors rapid, homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening, thereby yielding densely packed, micron-sized grains with minimized grain boundary area and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min in N₂ fully volatilizes residual DMSO, drives complete ligand exchange, relieves lattice strain as confirmed by the absence of PbI₂ residuals (XRD peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) perovskite reflection, and promotes Br⁻ incorporation into the lattice to passivate iodide vacancies and reduce halide migration pathways—collectively evidenced by uniform film coverage and high grayscale intensity across optical micrographs, intense and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence emission with prolonged carrier lifetime (>1.2 µs) in time-resolved PL mapping, and coherent XRD peak sharpening indicating low microstrain and high phase purity; these morphological, optical, and structural signatures jointly corroborate a near-ideal crystallization trajectory wherein interfacial trap states are intrinsically suppressed, charge extraction barriers are minimized, and bulk recombination is curtailed—culminating in VOC of 1.0353 V, JSC of 23.717 mA/cm², FF of 65.3602%, and PCE of 16.0482%.
